correctness.rationale: Independent exact enumeration grouped all 15 integer line-pair cross products per arrangement by primitive projective coordinates, then evaluated x²+y²−25z² at those points. For Q₁ the conic contains two classes of three lines and one of two lines; for Q₂ it contains two of three and two of two. The dual-conic tests 25a²+25b²−c² are (9,9,625,16,484,16) and (9,25,9,16,16,625), hence all intersections with the conic are transverse. Bézout gives 12 line–conic incidences each, leaving respectively 4 and 2 nodes after subtracting the multiple classes; these residual points cannot be shared by two lines or they would have occurred in the line-pair census. Thus the profiles are (4,1,2) and (2,2,2), while t₂,t₃,t₄=(6,3,2) for both. For each line, count its distinct projective classes and add 2 minus its number of classes on the conic. The respective counts are (4,3,3,5,4,3) and (3,6,3,4,4,3); adding the conic counts 7 and 6 yields the stated r_j. The degree map identifies the unique conic, so its profile alone obstructs equivalent W_C. The weak claim uses the published mdr values 4 and 3; no new syzygy computation was made. Reviewed RESULT.md lines 28–56 and VERIFICATION.md; the independent replay (independent_incidence_replay.py) used the procedure above, not the uploaded verifier. There is no claim about other realizations or other characteristics.
